Standard reduction: given graph G=(V,E) and integer k for independent set, transform to same graph G and set k' = n - k for vertex cover. Because complement of independent set is vertex cover. Indeed, a set S is independent of size >= k iff V \ S is a vertex cover of size <= n - k. So reduction is trivial: same n, same edges, new k = n - k_original.

Edge cases: need to ensure mapping works for all cases. For k <=0 original always yes; then n - k >= n, which is >= n, and vertex cover with k' >= n is always yes (since all vertices cover). That matches. For k > n original always no; then n - k < 0, vertex cover with k' negative is always no. Good.

class IndependentSet:
    """Independent Set.

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
      * k is any integer.

    Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
    vertices with no edge between any two of them.

    Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
    every set of vertices is independent.
    """

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        validate_graph_with_k(instance)


class VertexCover:
    """Vertex Cover.

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
      * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
        [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
      * k is any integer.

    vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

    k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
